about.title: Inglewood Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Inglewood is a city of roughly 111,000 people packed into busy blocks along Century Boulevard, Manchester Boulevard, Prairie Avenue and La Brea Avenue. Those corridors carry storefronts, parking structures, apartment complexes, event crowds and foot traffic all day long. When a floor is left wet, a stairwell light burns out, a walkway cracks or a spill sits unattended, the person who ends up hurt is rarely the one who created the problem. California premises liability law asks a specific question: did the property owner or manager know about the hazard, or should they have known, and did they fail to fix it or warn you? Proving that notice is where most of these claims are won or lost, which is why what you do in the first days matters so much. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects injured Inglewood residents and visitors with an independent attorney who can evaluate the property, request surveillance footage before it is overwritten, and pursue a claim on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Inglewood Residents Turn to LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Notice Is the Heart of the Case
items.desc: In California you generally have to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and did nothing. Attorneys in our network know how to look for inspection logs, prior complaints and maintenance records that establish that knowledge.

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than People Expect
items.desc: Most premises claims carry a two-year filing deadline, but if the property belongs to a city, county or other public entity, the window to file a claim is far shorter. Getting connected early protects your options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so being partly to blame reduces a recovery rather than erasing it. An attorney can push back when a property owner tries to pin the entire fall on you.

items.question: I fell in a store on Century Boulevard in Inglewood and the manager said cameras would be checked. Should I do anything else?
items.answer: Yes. Many businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks, so an attorney can send a written preservation request right away. In the meantime, photograph the exact spot, your shoes, and any signage or lack of it, and write down the names of employees or customers who saw what happened. Keep the clothes you were wearing unwashed if they show the spill or debris.

items.question: What if I slipped on a public sidewalk or in a city-owned building?
items.answer: Claims against a public entity in California follow a different and much faster process than claims against a private owner, with a formal claim required well before the standard two-year deadline. Missing that early step can bar the case entirely. Because of that, it is worth speaking with an attorney as soon as you can rather than waiting to see how your injuries develop.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything, and am I obligated to hire the attorney?
items.answer: LawProactive is free and we are not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who reviews your fall at no charge, and you decide whether to move forward. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, which means there is no fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
